# VerifyError causes in translated Android bytecode (AlertDialogLayout.onMeasure case)

> Source discipline: JVMS / OpenJDK / AndroidX / developer.android.com statements are official-spec facts with links. Isakai-translator statements are working-translator lore or local observations, labeled as such. No new harness code was created; all workflow steps use stock `javap`/`java` tooling (verified on Temurin JDK 27 in this session).

## Top causes of VerifyError in generated bytecode

### Takeaway
For a translator emitting major v49 (like Isakai's), StackMapTable is not the failure mode — v49 verifies by inference with no frames; the top causes are uninitialized-object misuse, long/double slot discipline, branch-merge type mismatches, and wrong method/field descriptors. StackMapTable defects only dominate at v50+.

### Cited Findings
- Class files with version < 50.0 verify by type inference; verification by type checking (StackMapTable) must be used at version >= 50.0 — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- Fallback from failed type-checking to inference is allowed if and only if the version equals exactly 50.0, described as a transitional accommodation for tools that rewrite bytecode without fixing frames — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10.1](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- StackMapTable attribute is versioned 50.0 / Java 6, i.e. it does not exist as a verification vehicle below v50 — [JVMS SE 17, Table 4.7-C](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- An `invokespecial` naming `<init>` requires the target on the stack to be an *uninitialized* instance; `<init>` must never be invoked on an initialized instance, and an uninitialized current-class instance restricts which `<init>` may be named — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10.1.8–4.10.1.9 (invokespecial rules)](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- `long`/`double` occupy two local-variable slots; the second slot is marked reserved/"must not be used", and overwriting either half poisons the neighbor slot — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10.2.3](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- `Uninitialized_variable_info` carries the offset of the `new` that created the object; `UninitializedThis` is a distinct verification type — [JVMS SE 17, §4.7.4](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- HotSpot's verifier reports, among others: `"Bad type on operand stack in %s"`, `"Bad type on operand stack in putfield"`, `"Bad <init> method call"`, `"Bad operand type when invoking <init>"`, `"Bad access to protected data in %s"`, `"Inconsistent args count operand in invokeinterface"`, `"Stack map does not match the one at "` — [OpenJDK verifier.cpp](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/hotspot/share/classfile/verifier.cpp)
- `VerifyError` is thrown when the verifier detects a class file violating the language or VM constraints — [VerifyError javadoc, Java SE 17](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/VerifyError.html)
- (Working-translator lore, Isakai C6 history) Recurring local VerifyError roots: `iaload` emitted for a `float[]` (fixed by descriptor-aware array-component analysis via `sget/iget-object` field types + `aget-object` dimension peeling); forward-ctor `iload` used for float/double params (fixed to `fload`/`dload`); receiver narrowing to `java/lang/Object` breaking protected access (`B0/a.values()` "Bad access to protected data" — fixed by always skipping Object-narrowing) — (local observation: `progress/archive/C6-translator-framework-failures.md` lines ~933, ~948, ~984)

### Inferences
- A translator that stays on major v49 (Isakai does — see next section) trades StackMapTable bugs for inference bugs: every branch merge, JSR-free inlined finally, and uninitialized-object pairing must be exactly right because there are no frames to paper over them, and there is no v49 fallback (fallback only exists *at* 50.0).
- Wrong descriptors (e.g. `(Ljava/lang/String;)V` vs `()Ljava/lang/String;`, int-vs-float array opcodes) are the cheapest VerifyError to produce and the cheapest to fix: they fail fast at the use site with "Bad type on operand stack".

### Gaps
- No reliable public corpus ranks VerifyError causes by frequency in DEX-to-class translators specifically; the ranking above is inferred from JVMS constraint density plus local Isakai history, not a published statistic.
- Whether Temurin-27 (the JDK used here) still honors the v50.0 inference fallback could not be confirmed from reachable docs; Isakai's v49 strategy does not depend on it.

## Reading a VerifyError message (offset + expected vs actual)

### Takeaway
A HotSpot VerifyError names the *method*, the *kind* of mismatch, and usually the bytecode offset plus expected/actual types; map the offset with `javap -c` and confirm the merge/frame state with `javap -v`.

### Cited Findings
- HotSpot verifier messages embed the failure site and types, e.g. `"Bad type on operand stack in %s"`, `"Expecting a stack map frame"`, `"Expecting new instruction"`, `"Bad stack map offset %d"`, `"Stack map does not match the one at "` — [OpenJDK verifier.cpp](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/hotspot/share/classfile/verifier.cpp)
- A typical HotSpot message has the shape `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack in <method> ... bci=@<offset> ... expected <X> but found <Y>` (message-format lore widely reproduced from verifier.cpp `verify_error` call sites; exact wording varies by check) — [OpenJDK verifier.cpp](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/blob/master/src/hotspot/share/classfile/verifier.cpp)
- `javap -c` prints bytecode with offsets (`0: iload_1`, `1: ifle 9`, …) and `javap -v` prints `StackMapTable: number_of_entries = N` with per-frame `frame_type`/`locals`/`stack` — (local observation: demonstrated this session on Temurin 27, `--release 8` class shows major 52 with 2 frames; see workflow below)
- `javap -verify` prints additional class verification info for the class being disassembled — (local observation: `javap -help` on Temurin 27 lists `-verify`)

### Inferences
- Diagnosis procedure from the message alone: (1) class+method names scope the search; (2) `bci=@N` is the failing instruction — find offset N in `javap -c`; (3) "expected vs actual" tells whether the producer (wrong opcode/descriptor) or the merge (branch joining two types) is at fault; (4) "Expecting a stack map frame" / "Stack map does not match" at v50+ points at the frame in `javap -v` output for the branch target, not at the instruction itself.
- For Isakai's v49 output, "Expecting a stack map frame" should never be the primary error; if it appears, suspect a tool in the chain (e.g. a post-processor) stamped v50+ on the class, not the translator's own emission.

### Gaps
- HotSpot message wording is version-sensitive (JDK 17 vs 27 phrasing drifts); I did not diff verifier.cpp across releases, so quote exact strings from the running JDK's source before scripting a parser.
- No official document exhaustively lists every verifier message string; verifier.cpp is the de-facto reference.

## Translator patterns that most often produce VerifyErrors

### Takeaway
Missing/wrong frames (v50+ only), inlined try/catch/finally without JSR discipline, and descriptor/signature confusion are the classic translator-introduced failures; Isakai's v49 + register-map design replaces the first with register-type-tracking bugs.

### Cited Findings
- The JVMS itself calls out the tool-rewriter failure: bytecode-altering tools that do not adjust stack map frames fail type checking on bytecodes that would pass under inference — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10.1](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- Compilers targeting ≤ 50.0 implement try–finally with `jsr`/`ret` subroutines; the verifier has dedicated inference rules for them (§4.10.2.5), so inlining or duplicating finally blocks without preserving subroutine discipline breaks inference — [JVMS SE 17, §4.10.2.5](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- `Signature` attributes (generics) are versioned 49.0 / Java 5 and verification *ignores* unknown/signature-level attributes for type-checking purposes — signatures do not cause VerifyError; the erased descriptor does — [JVMS SE 17, Table 4.7-C](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jvms/se17/html/jvms-4.html)
- (Working-translator lore) Isakai emits major v49 explicitly so that "pure inference verification" applies and "frames [are] never required (JDK 27 enforces frames at v50)" — (local observation: `src/translate.zig`, `writeU16(&out, gpa, 49)` comment; `dexFlagsToJvm` accessor mapping at the same site)
- (Working-translator lore) Isakai tracks DEX registers to JVM locals with a `RegMap`/type array where stores do *not* clear pending new-instance types, on the theory that a valid DEX `<init>` call's object is always its dominating `new` — (local observation: `src/translate.zig`, `storeTracked` comment)
- (Working-translator lore) The translator previously narrowed receivers to `java/lang/Object`, which broke protected-member access verification; the fix is to never Object-narrow since every reference is already assignable — (local observation: `progress/archive/C6-translator-framework-failures.md` ~line 948)

### Inferences
- For the concrete `AlertDialogLayout.onMeasure` case, the suspect list ordered by likelihood under a v49 DEX translator: (a) branch-merge mismatch across the many early-return / panel-null joins in `tryOnMeasure` (int vs reference, or two unrelated panel types meeting in one local); (b) wrong descriptor on a `measure`/`getMeasuredHeight`/`combineMeasuredStates` call or a narrowed receiver tripping protected access; (c) mishandled `new`+`<init>` pairing for `MeasureSpec` boxing or similar temporaries across the duplicated measure passes. StackMapTable and generic signatures are unlikely roots — the former cannot exist at v49, the latter is ignored by the verifier.
- The `storeTracked` "stores do not clear pending new-instance types" invariant is exactly the kind of inference-sensitive shortcut to re-examine first if the error mentions `<init>`/uninitialized at this method.

### Gaps
- The actual failing `AlertDialogLayout.onMeasure` VerifyError text and `javap -c` dump were not in the reachable repo history (only referenced as N6 blocker "(2) abort message hidden by VerifyError in translated layout code"); the ranked suspect list above is therefore a prior, not a confirmed diagnosis.
- No citable source quantifies how often inlined try/catch vs descriptor bugs dominate across DEX translators generally.

## Minimal verification workflow (javap + stackmap inspection)

### Takeaway
`javap -c` locates the failing offset, `javap -v` shows frames (or their v49 absence), and a targeted re-translation closes the loop — all with stock JDK tooling, no harness code.

### Cited Findings
- `javap -c` disassembles code with per-instruction offsets; `-v` adds the constant pool, version numbers, and per-method `StackMapTable` entries; `-verify` adds verification info — (local observation: `javap -help`, Temurin 27)
- Correct `AlertDialogLayout.onMeasure` behavior: `onMeasure` delegates to `tryOnMeasure`, falling back to `super.onMeasure` on false; `tryOnMeasure` classifies children by id (`topPanel` exactly wrap_content; content/custom at most fill_parent with first priority for extra space; button panel minHeight..wrap_content with second priority), measures each panel with derived `MeasureSpec`s, and must end with measured dimensions set — [AlertDialogLayout.java, androidx-main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/androidx/androidx/androidx-main/appcompat/appcompat/src/main/java/androidx/appcompat/widget/AlertDialogLayout.java)
- `onMeasure(int, int)` is the "determine the size requirements for this view and all of its children" callback in the View layout protocol — [View reference, developer.android.com](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/View.html#onMeasure(int,%20int))
- A minimal method with a branch merge compiles to offsets with 2 `StackMapTable` entries at v52 (`frame_type = 9 /* same */`, `frame_type = 252 /* append */ locals = [ int ]`) — (local observation: `Demo.f` compiled `--release 8`, `javap -v` this session)

### Inferences
- Workflow (all stock tooling):
  1. `java <translated-class>` (or the app launch) captures the full `VerifyError: ... in <Class>.<method> ... bci=@N` text.
  2. `javap -c -p -cp <translated-classes-dir> <Class> > /tmp/before.txt`; find offset N in the failing method; list which branches join there and what each pushes/stores.
  3. `javap -v -p -cp <dir> <Class> | grep -A8 'FailingMethod\|StackMapTable'` — at v49 expect *no* StackMapTable (confirms the inference path); at v50+ compare the frame at the branch target against the actual locals/stack from step 2.
  4. Cross-check the call descriptors at N against AOSP/AndroidX source (`AlertDialogLayout` above; `View.combineMeasuredStates`, `MeasureSpec.makeMeasureSpec` signatures) — a narrowed receiver or int/float confusion shows here.
  5. Fix the translator emission (descriptor map, register-type tracking, or branch-local typing), re-translate, repeat steps 1–3; proof is `VerifyError` gone *plus* the method's measured behavior matching the contract (three-panel distribution per the class doc), not just class-load success.
- This workflow uses only `java`/`javap` plus public source reads, satisfying the no-new-harness constraint.

### Gaps
- `javap -verify` output format on Temurin 27 was not exercised against a genuinely failing translated class in this session (no failing class file was at hand); the exact extra lines it prints for this case remain unconfirmed.
- The "correct behavior" bar for the translated method (pixel-level panel distribution) needs the live app flow to prove; class-load success alone is necessary but not sufficient.
